{{Quote|&hellip;Biting metal and stinging light&hellip;|Excerpt from the Sith tome that inspired the creation of Lumiya's lightwhip|<ref name="LDSE" />}}
'''Lumiya's lightwhip''' was the personal weapon of choice used in combat by [[Lumiya]], [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lady of the Sith]]. Lumiya crafted her [[Lightwhip/Legends|lightwhip]], a device of ancient [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] design, after she found an [[Sith scroll/Legends|instructional tome]] during her pilgrimage to the [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]], which spoke of a scourge that included both tangible extensions and coherent [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] energy. The then&ndash;[[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] forged the [[Hilt/Legends|hilt]] of her lightwhip out of near-indestructible [[Beskar/Legends|Mandalorian iron]] and powered it with shards of [[Kaiburr crystal]] gifted to her by her [[Sith Master/Legends|Master]], the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]].

Lumiya first revealed her signature weapon during the onset of the [[Nagai–Tof War]] against her archenemy, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], whom she defeated in their [[Skirmish on Kinooine#First encounter|initial confrontation]] on the planet [[Kinooine/Legends|Kinooine]]. Skywalker later bested the Dark Lady in a [[Skirmish on Kinooine#Rematch|rematch]] on the same battleground after he discovered that the combination of a standard lightsaber and its [[Shoto lightsaber/Legends|short-bladed version]] was able to sufficiently negate the advantage of her lightwhip's dual nature. Lumiya brandished her trademark flail for nearly the next four decades, eliciting fear with its mere mention and maiming or [[Death/Legends|killing]] those opponents who got caught in its tendrils. Her lightwhip served as a note of contention for many [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] over the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] as well, but none so much as her long-time rival, Luke Skywalker. In [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], Lumiya utilized her lightwhip for a final time against him in a [[Duel on Terephon|duel]] on the planet [[Terephon]]. Forsaking the advantage of his shoto, Skywalker defeated the Dark Lady of the Sith with only his lightsaber and killed her with a [[Sai cha/Legends|decapitating strike]] as her lightwhip fell into the chasm below the precipice on which they fought.

==Description==
===Design===
{{Quote|But only some of your whip's tendrils are of energy. Others of them are corporeal, formed of metal, or of hides.|Den Siva|<ref name="SW96" />}}
[[File:LumiyasLightwhipHilt-SW1977-96.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The hilt of Lumiya's lightwhip]]
[[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lady of the Sith]]<ref name="EGTTF" /> [[Lumiya]]'s signature accoutrement, the [[Lightwhip/Legends|lightwhip]], was a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] weapon that produced beams of pliant energy in conjunction with physical matter.<ref name="Tempest" /> Its tubular [[Hilt/Legends|hilt]] was forged from nearly-indestructible<ref name="DLOTS 2">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 2]]</ref> [[Beskar/Legends|Mandalorian iron]] and was powered by shards of [[Kaiburr crystal]] given to her by her [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Master]],<ref name="lumiyadatabank" /> then&ndash;Dark Lord of the Sith<ref name="Fall">''[[The Rise and Fall of Darth Vader]]''</ref>  [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]].<ref name="lumiyadatabank" /> While lightwhips operated by other individuals only produced single flexible blades of [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] energy,<ref name="lightwhip">The [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Githany]] wielded a [[Lightwhip/Legends|lightwhip]] with a single strand of [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]-type energy in [[Star Wars: Jedi vs. Sith|''Jedi vs. Sith'']].</ref><ref name="lightwhip2">[[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Jax Pavan]] also wielded a lightwhip with a single strand of [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]-type energy against [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]] in ''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''.</ref> Lumiya's was quite unique in that it had three separate extension types: along with several filaments of [[Color/Legends|yellow]] [[Plasma/Legends|plasma]], the weapon included multiple extensions of [[Leather/Legends|leather]] studded with [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Iron/Legends|iron]]<ref name="Sacrifice" /> and flexible gem-speckled metal.<ref name="Tempest" /> Lumiya kept spare parts for the whip, including additional shards of Kaiburr [[Crystal/Legends|crystal]], locked within a storage room in her [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] [[The Home|home]] near [[Bimmiel/Legends|Bimmiel]].<ref name="Inferno">''[[Legacy of the Force: Inferno]]''</ref>

===Utilization===
{{Quote|How does it work?''"<br />"''On the same principle as my whip&hellip;when you activate that stud on the hilt, it releases a beam of coherent energy which forms the sword blade.|Lumiya explains the similarities between a lightsaber and her lightwhip to Den Siva|<ref name="SW96" />}}
Lumiya usually held her whip with the extensions coiled when not in use.<ref name="SW96" /><ref name="SW95" /> Other times, she wore it around her waist like a belt,<ref name="Exile">''[[Legacy of the Force: Exile]]''</ref> or even concealed the whip within one of her [[Cybernetics/Legends|mechanical legs]].<ref name="Betrayal">''[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]''</ref> It had an equal number of each of the three extension types<ref name="Tempest" /> and a range of up to six [[Meter/Legends|meters]],<ref name="tep" /> although there was the potential to retract them into the hilt to effect better control.<ref name="Tempest" /> The lightwhip could have also wielded any one of the three types singularly and independently of the others.<ref name="SW95" /> It operated in the same manner as a traditional lightsaber in that a [[Activation stud|switch]] was required on the hilt to activate the weapon's energy portion.<ref name="SW96" /> When the energy extensions of her lightwhip were used, the weapon resonated with a snap-hiss similar in sound to that produced by a lightsaber.<ref name="Tempest" /> Its [[white]]-hot beams had the ability to rend [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]],<ref name="Sacrifice" /> and cleave body parts, organic<ref name="Tempest" /> or otherwise.<ref name="Sacrifice" /> Severe wounds could also have been inflicted by the extensions even after the whip was deactivated.<ref name="Wounds">In ''[[Legacy of the Force: Tempest]]'', [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Alema Rar]] suffered serious wounds from the energy filaments of Lumiya's whip even after they had been deactivated.</ref>

===Advantages===
{{Quote|That combination is what defeated him. His Jedi training had prepared him for an energy weapon, or a solid one. Not one that was both at once.|Lumiya, explaining the advantages of her whip|<ref name="SW96" />}}
[[File:LukeGetsHisButtWhipped.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Luke Skywalker, overwhelmed by the strands of Lumiya's lightwhip]]
The more common lightwhip was already a rare and exotic weapon, and its solitary, flexible, energy appendage&mdash;while less powerful than a lightsaber&mdash;was an unfamiliar occurrence among traditional lightsaber adepts. Because of that, lightwhip masters usually enjoyed a considerable amount of leverage over their foes.<ref name="advantage">In ''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]'', the [[Sith Blademaster|Blademaster]] [[Kas'im]] explains to [[Darth Bane/Legends|Bane]] that while [[Githany]]'s [[Lightwhip/Legends|lightwhip]] is less powerful than a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], her advantage comes from her opponent's unfamiliarity with it.</ref> However, the one-of-a-kind construction of Lumiya's whip afforded her an even greater advantage when fighting against lightsaber-equipped opponents, especially those who had no prior experience in dealing with lightwhips and were thus confused by the dual nature of her exclusive weapon.<ref name="Betrayal" />

The range of the lightwhip's extensions allowed Lumiya to attack her enemies from a vantage point of several meters; that made it extremely difficult for them to closely engage the Dark Lady and allowed her to maintain control of combat situations.<ref name="SW96" /> The whip's tails could have splayed in a vertical attack pattern, which allowed Lumiya to strike high, midway, and low all at once. Conversely, fanning the whip's tresses out in a horizontal flourish gave it the appearance of a weaponized cloud,<ref name="Betrayal" /> in a maneuver that prevented contenders from sidestepping to evade the impending assault.<ref name="Tempest" /> Attempting to defend oneself by twirling a lightsaber into a shielding arc was also useless, because the lightwhip's reach extended over and beyond the length of the blade.<ref name="Betrayal" /> If her guard was somehow penetrated, Lumiya was able to use the whip like a short lightsaber to parry incoming attacks, and she had the ability to even handle it like a staff to block the blades of adversaries.<ref name="Sacrifice" />

===Inadequacies===
{{Quote|Two blades&mdash;one long and one short?''"<br />"''Against the two natures of your weapon.|Lumiya and Luke Skywalker|<ref name="SW96" />}}
Lumiya's lightwhip could be defeated by a warrior skilled in the [[Jar'Kai/Legends|Jar'Kai dueling style]]<ref name="Tempest" /> who was furnished with both a standard lightsaber and a short-bladed variation known as a [[Shoto lightsaber/Legends|shoto]].<ref name="SW96" /> Furthermore, while the whip's hilt was forged from an indestructible [[Ore/Legends|ore]],<ref name="LDSE" /> its extensions were not. The whip's metal and leather thongs were vulnerable to being cut, and the energy beams had the potential to short out violently if sufficient force was applied with a lightsaber.<ref name="SW96" /> By ensnaring the whip's plasma energy with the longer lightsaber, an individual had the ability to use his or her shoto to shred the whip's metal and leather cords.<ref name="Tempest" /> After the tangible extensions were eliminated, Lumiya's challenger could have then focused on the destruction of the whip's energy beams.<ref name="SW96" />

It was also possible for an individual with a single lightsaber to overcome Lumiya's lightwhip through superior combat finesse against the Dark Lady. On one occasion, patience, cunning, and capitalization on Lumiya's mistakes allowed an opponent to avoid the whip and come within striking range of its owner.<ref name="Tempest" /> The use of speed to eliminate the whip's ability to gather sufficient swinging momentum and brute force to hammer at its master's defenses was also an effective offensive combination. Certain projectile weapons, such as a [[Flechette launcher/Legends|flechette launcher]], rendered the lightwhip's copious range obsolete, and strong [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-[[Telekinesis/Legends|pushes]] were even able to slow the speed of the whip cracks.<ref name="Sacrifice" />

==History==
===A Sith weapon===
{{Quote|You know what I can do with this.|Lumiya threatens Faron Tolis with her whip|<ref name="SW95" />}}
[[File:Lumiya_by_Bruno_Werneck.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Lumiya uses her lightwhip against New Republic soldiers.]]
Before completing her [[Sith training|training]] as the [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] of then&ndash;Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Vader, Lumiya was tasked with the creation of her own weapon. She embarked on a sojourn<ref name="LDSE" /> to the Sith world of [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]],<ref name="lumiyadatabank" /> where she uncovered an ancient [[Sith scroll/Legends|relic]] that spoke of a weapon that included both lightsaber energy and corporeal matter. It was upon this foundation that Lumiya crafted her lightwhip.<ref name="LDSE" />

The lightwhip first saw action against a [[Belderone/Legends|Belderone]] native named [[Flint]], who Lumiya defeated in a vicious [[Duel on Vjun|duel]] on the planet [[Vjun/Legends|Vjun]].<ref name="end" /> Later [[4 ABY/Legends|that year]], the Dark Lady allied herself with the war-faring [[Nagai/Legends|Nagai]] [[Species/Legends|species]] in the midst of their [[Nagai–Tof War|invasion]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. While meeting with her [[Den Siva|''attaché'']], Lumiya intercepted a team of [[Alliance of Free Planets]] [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] who had been sent on a reconnaissance mission to the desolate world of [[Kinooine/Legends|Kinooine]]. Nineteen members of the twenty-person team were [[Death/Legends|killed]] by Lumiya's whip, and the sole survivor, [[Faron Tolis]], was repeatedly [[Torture/Legends|tortured]] with it.<ref name="TFW">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/nagai11202009/index.html|text=The Forgotten War: The Nagai and the Tofs|int=The Forgotten War: The Nagai and the Tofs}}</ref> When Alliance [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] arrived in search of Tolis' team, his two companions, [[Kiro]] and [[Dani/Legends|Dani]], were brutally attacked by a lightwhip-swinging Lumiya. Skywalker later attempted to avenge the assault on his friends when he [[Skirmish on Kinooine#First encounter|dueled]] Lumiya but was trounced because of his inexperience with facing someone who utilized a weapon of both substantial and intangible ends.<ref name="SW95" /> The weakness of her whip was soon discovered by Skywalker, who constructed and made use of a [[Luke Skywalker's shoto|red-bladed shoto]] along with his [[Luke Skywalker's green lightsaber/Legends|regular lightsaber]] in [[Skirmish on Kinooine#Rematch|his rematch]] with Lumiya. He destroyed much of it with his two blades before finally defeating her, much to her surprise.<ref name="SW96" />

Following the end of the Nagai-Tof War, Lumiya undertook a [[Assault on Epsilon Nine|mission]] on behalf of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] to the [[Communications Research Station|communications research]] [[Space station/Legends|space station]] [[Epsilon Nine]]. After successfully reinstating the traitorous inhabitant's commitment to the Empire, Lumiya used her whip to bisect a giant [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[Insignia of the New Republic|sigil]] that served as a symbol of the station staff's short-lived freedom. Soon afterward, her lightwhip was employed in a [[Confrontation on Caprioril|duel]] against rogue [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hand]] [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] on [[Caprioril]], which ended in a stalemate.<ref name="EGTTF" /> Lumiya went underground after her confrontation with Jade,<ref name="tep" /> but the memory of her infamous weapon was far from gone:<ref name="Betrayal" /> one of the many lessons taught to the [[Padawan/Legends|students]] of Luke Skywalker's [[New Jedi Order]] was the legend of the Sith Lady Lumiya and her peculiar choice of equipment.<ref name="Legend">In ''[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]'' and ''[[Legacy of the Force: Tempest]]'', [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]] and [[Alema Rar]] (respectively) remember being told of [[Lumiya]] and her [[Lightwhip/Legends|lightwhip]] during their days as apprentices.</ref>

===Later usage===
{{Quote|So I think it's time to break out my shoto.|Luke Skywalker, preparing to face Lumiya and her whip|<ref name="Tempest" />}}
As Lumiya returned to galactic prominence, so too did her notorious flail. In [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], she lured Skywalker's nephew, [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]], and another [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]], [[Nelani Dinn]], to her asteroid habitat in the [[MZX33291 system|MZX33291 star system]], where the whip was briefly wielded in a [[Duel at The Home|duel]] with Dinn. The Jedi [[Gender/Legends|girl]] had never before faced such a weapon and was flogged several times with it by Lumiya.<ref name="Betrayal" /> During the onset of the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], Lumiya traveled through the [[Coruscant Underworld/Legends|underlevels]] of the galactic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and killed several of the [[Feral (being)|transient inhabitants]] with her whip as she made her way to the [[Well of the World Brain]] to meet with Solo&mdash;now her Sith apprentice.<ref name="Tempest" />

The whip was later used in [[Duel in the Fellowship Plaza|combat]] against [[Chev]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Tresina Lobi]] on Coruscant in the [[Senate District/Legends|Senate District's]] [[Fellowship Plaza]]. Fanning its extensions kept Lobi at bay temporarily, but a combination of acrobatic maneuvers and distractions allowed the Chev Jedi to dodge the whip cracks before [[Cho sun/Legends|severing]] Lumiya's cybernetic weapon arm. Being ambidextrous, the Dark Lady continued to wield her lightwhip with her intact arm and used its ends to [[Cho mok/Legends|shear off]] both of Lobi's legs at the knee. The Jedi Master was killed immediately afterward by Lumiya's accomplice, the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[darksider]] [[Alema Rar]].<ref name="Tempest" />

Lumiya and her whip next appeared at the [[Roqoo Depot]] [[Fuel/Legends|refueling]] station, where she [[Duel on Roqoo Depot|fought]] with her nemesis, Luke Skywalker. Many of the station's patrons were seriously wounded, losing [[Limb/Legends|limbs]], heads, and their lives to the lashes of her lightwhip before the Jedi [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] finally took action against her, unveiling both his lightsaber and shoto to counter the whip's dual nature. He came within striking range, but the Dark Lady struck at his feet with the whip, depriving him of the opportunity to attack. He then used his two blades to meticulously begin cutting away the whip's strands as Lumiya thrashed at all angles, but she managed to land a critical strike that both [[Cho mai/Legends|severed his shoto-hand]] and slashed him about the chest. In preparation for the killing stroke, the Dark Lady shortened her whip's extensions for more precise control after using the energy tendrils to [[Sun djem/Legends|relieve]] Skywalker of his other lightsaber. She was defeated, however, after he shot her several times with a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]].<ref name="Tempest" /> Lumiya's lightwhip met Skywalker's twin blades again in [[Battle of Gilatter VIII|battle]] on [[Gilatter VIII]],<ref name="Exile" /> and that of his [[Marriage/Legends|wife]], Mara Jade Skywalker, soon afterward on the resort [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Hesperidium/Legends|Hesperidium]]. During [[Duel on Hesperidium|that duel]], Jade Skywalker was able to frustrate the whip's strikes by making use of blaster weapons before being ambushed by the [[Ship (Sith Meditation Sphere)|Sith Meditation Sphere]] under Lumiya's command.<ref name="Sacrifice" />

[[File:Lukekilllumiya.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Lumiya wields her lightwhip for a final time.]]
Lumiya's lightwhip saw its final usage on the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] world [[Terephon]], when the Dark Lady again entered into [[Duel on Terephon|single combat]] with Luke Skywalker. Eschewing the use of his shoto, Skywalker implemented an aggressive two-handed onslaught against the whip's linear assault. Lumiya was unable to achieve its maximum velocity when Skywalker rushed her, forcing the Dark Lady to give ground as she attempted to regain sufficient distance to effectively swing her weapon. She held its hilt like a staff to block Skywalker's blows, but this too was ineffective. He ended the [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|duel]] by [[Sai cha/Legends|decapitating]] Lumiya, while her lightwhip tumbled down into the gorge below the cliff on which they fought.<ref name="Sacrifice" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:LumiyaLightwhipRebelScum.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Lumiya's lightwhip-equipped Hasbro action figure]]
Lumiya's lightwhip first appeared in the ''[[Star Wars (1977)|Marvel Star Wars']]'' ninety-fifth [[Star Wars comic books|issue]], [[Star Wars (1977) 95|''No Zeltrons'']], written by [[Mary Jo Duffy]]. The whip was penciled by artist [[Cynthia Martin]], originally appearing only as an energy weapon.<ref name="SW95" /> In the following issue, [[Star Wars (1977) 96|''Duel With a Dark Lady'']], Duffy and Martin revealed that the whip included corporeal elements along with energy, all of which originated from a cylindrical hilt design.<ref name="SW96" /> The actual ''Star Wars 96: Duel With a Dark Lady'' comic was re-released in [[2009]] in a package that included action figures of Lumiya with her lightwhip, as well as Luke Skywalker and both of his lightsabers for [[Hasbro]]'s ''[[Star Wars: The Legacy Collection]]'' series.<ref name="HasbroToy">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Legacy Collection|packtype=''Star Wars'' Comic Pack|pack=#07: Lumiya & Luke Skywalker (Marvel's ''Star Wars'' #96)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/tlccomicpackslc07.asp}}</ref>

The backstory for the whip's creation was fleshed out in [[Michael Mikaelian]]'s short story titled ''[[Lumiya: Dark Star of the Empire]]'', which was featured in [[Star Wars Galaxy Magazine 3|''Star Wars Galaxy Magazine'' 3]].<ref name="LDSE" /> The whip's origins were also touched upon in several pieces of source material, including ''[[Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties]]'',<ref name="end" /> ''[[The Emperor's Pawns]]'',<ref name="tep" /> [[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']] (in which artist [[Tommy Lee Edwards]] distinctly depicts the whip with a curved hilt),<ref name="EGTTF" /> and [[2008]]'s ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|265|Lumiya}}</ref> The lightwhip was prominently featured with its owner in several of the ''[[Star Wars: Legacy of the Force]]'' novels: ''[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]'',<ref name="Betrayal" /> ''[[Legacy of the Force: Tempest]]'',<ref name="Tempest" /> ''[[Legacy of the Force: Exile]]'',<ref name="Exile" /> and ''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''.<ref name="Sacrifice" /> An action figure of Lumiya and her lightwhip is included in the [[Legacy of the Force (Star Wars Miniatures)|''Legacy of the Force'']] set of ''[[Star Wars Miniatures]]''.
